body.statement: For any sequence of accepted effective certificates with \(\varepsilon_n\le\overline\varepsilon_n\to0\), let \(C_{n,\alpha}=Q^+_{n,\alpha}+\sqrt{\overline\varepsilon_n}+\zeta\). Then \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)}P_n\{T_n(t)\le C_{n,\alpha}\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\}\ge1-\alpha\). For every operational selector \(\widehat t_n\) that is \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable, including every Borel-measurable choice based on \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\), \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)}P_n\{T_n(\widehat t_n)\le C_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\). At an interior selected value this event is exactly \(\{(1+\widehat c_n)\sqrt n\,\mathscr R_n(\widehat c_n)\le C_{n,\alpha}\}\), where \(\widehat c_n=\widehat t_n/(1-\widehat t_n)\). The plug-in frontier is used only to generate the observed-data selector; coverage concerns the oracle normalized regret path. The conclusion uses one-sided ramps and the verified lower CDF bracket and does not assume continuity of the distribution of \(S(h,Z_V)\).
body.justification: This is the operational selection-valid coverage theorem: the selected temperature is computed from observed data, while the covered quantity is the oracle causal regret, and validity remains correct at exact ties and quantile atoms.
body.gap: CCK and Giessing anti-concentration results apply to Gaussian-process suprema, Fang--Santos quantile validity requires regularity not supplied at atoms, and none states the observed-selector-to-oracle-regret bridge for a nonlinear causal frontier.
body.consumer: A planner may inspect the sample-computable welfare--divergence frontier, choose a temperature measurably from it, and report a certified upper bound for the oracle regret at that chosen point.
